land.text: the Imamate 'overthrown by the Russian Empire' in 1859, after Shamil accepted surrender terms

successors.note: The infobox also lists a 'Mountain Republic' as successor, which is the 1917-1920 state, not the 1859 handover.

capitals.name: Gimry
capitals.note: Infobox: Gimry 'under Ghazi Muhammad'. Years are the imam's reign (1828-1832); the page gives no capital years. Coordinates from the Gimry page (42°45′26″N 46°50′44″E, Untsukulsky District); Reviewer eu-19-f corrected them from an approximate 42.4 N 46.85 E.

capitals.name: Khunzakh (also Gotsatl)
capitals.note: Infobox: Gotsatl and Khunzakh 'under Hamzat Bek' (reign 1832-1834). Coordinates approximate.

capitals.name: Dargo (Shamil's seats: Ashilta, Akhulgo, Dargo, Vedeno)
capitals.note: Infobox lists Ashilta, Akhulgo, Dargo and Vedeno under Imam Shamil without years; the dot sits at Dargo (the Caucasian War page gives an 1841 congress at Dargo). Coordinates approximate.

rulers.name: Ghazi Muhammad
rulers.title: Imam
rulers.note: Infobox 1828-1832; Gimry fell to Velyaminov in October 1832 and Ghazi Muhammad died.

rulers.name: Shamil
rulers.title: Imam
rulers.note: 'He led the mountaineers from 1834 until his capture by Dmitry Milyutin in 1859' (Caucasian War page).

minus.text: the Avar Khanate round Khunzakh, 'the capital of the Khanate of Avaria', attacked in vain in 1827 and joined only under Hamzat Bek

correction.text: For 1828-1831: the 1828 shape without the Avar Khanate (radius 40 km round Khunzakh, my estimate). From 1832 the whole 1828 shape holds (new keyframe 1832).

keyframe_review.note: 38,173 km2; the page has no area, so none to compare. The shape reaches 46.7 E, so it includes Khunzakh, yet the page says Ghazi Muhammad's attack on Khunzakh failed in 1827 and that Hamzat Bek (1832-1834) 'had secured the Avar Khanate's allegiance'. The 1828-1831 core was the imam's mountain communities of northern Dagestan ('renewed their campaign in northern Dagestan'); the page does not draw it, so the Avar disc is a rough subtraction.

correction.text: the whole 1828 shape, Avaria included, from Hamzat Bek's reign: 'had secured the Avar Khanate's allegiance'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, years only: the Cliopatria 1828 shape unchanged for 1832-1835. The page dates Hamzat Bek 1832-1834 and Shamil from 1834; it does not date the Avar allegiance within 1832-1834.

34,869 km2, 3,304 km2 less than 1828-1835. UNVERIFIED: page budget. Neither page records a loss in 1836; the Caucasian War page quotes Kaziev (1997) that the Imamate 'included virtually all of Nagorno-Dagestan' and all of Chechnya except the Terek-Suzhna strip, and Dadaev (2006) that it absorbed 'the lands of the liquidated Avar Khanate', which fits a shape of this size. Shamil took 'every Russian outpost in Avaria except one' after 28 August 1843.

34,869 km2, the same polygon as 1836-1856. UNVERIFIED: page budget. The Caucasian War page has a 250,000-strong army under Baryatinsky breaking 'the mountaineers' resistance' between 1856 and 1859, with no sequence of lost districts; Cliopatria draws no loss, so the shape probably overstates the Imamate in 1857-1858. A gap-filler should open Imam Shamil and the Fall of Gunib.

correction.text: the 1857 shape carried to the year of the surrender: 'Shamil accepted, dissolving the Imamate' in 1859

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria stops the Imamate in 1858; the infobox gives 'Overthrown by the Russian Empire: 1859' and the Caucasian War page puts Shamil's capture in 1859. The extent in 1859 is the 1857 shape, unverified.

region.text: northern Dagestan, where the imams 'renewed their campaign' in 1828 and Ghazi Muhammad 'proclaimed himself the first leader'

ledger.note: 1828: the Gazawat begins and the Imamate is established to combat the Russians. Infobox 'The Gazawat begins, the Imamate is established to combat the Russians: 1828'. The page names northern Dagestan and gives no month; the Cliopatria shape is the 1828 extent. The infobox lists a 'Chechen Dominion' before it.

region.text: the Khanate of Avaria round Khunzakh, whose allegiance Hamzat Bek 'had secured' in 1832-1834

ledger.note: 1832-1834: Hamzat Bek brings the Avar Khanate into the Imamate. 'Hamzat Bek had previously secured the allegiance of the Avar Khanate' (imam 1832-1834); he was assassinated in 1834. The page does not pick a year inside the span; 1832 is the start of his reign. Ghazi Muhammad's and Shamil's 1827 attack on Khunzakh had failed.

region.text: Avaria: after Untsukul on 28 August 1843, 'Shamil captured every Russian outpost in Avaria except one' over the next four weeks

ledger.note: 1843: Shamil sweeps the Russian posts out of Avaria. 'On 28 August 1843, 10,000 men converged from three different directions, on a Russian column in Untsukul, killing 486 men'; the outposts fell in the following four weeks (to September). Month 8 is the battle; the region is my reading of 'Avaria'.

region.text: the Imamate 'overthrown by the Russian Empire' when Shamil surrendered

ledger.note: 1859: Shamil surrenders and the Imamate falls. 'In 1859, after decades of resistance, Emperor Alexander II of Russia offered Shamil honorable surrender terms'; 'Shamil accepted, dissolving the Imamate.' The pages give no month or day.

wars.name: Caucasian War
wars.outcome: Russian victory over the Imamate: Shamil led the mountaineers 'from 1834 until his capture by Dmitry Milyutin in 1859'. A truce in 1853-1856 ended with 'hostilities resumed in 1855'; a 250,000-strong army under Baryatinsky 'broke the mountaineers' resistance' in 1856-1859.
wars.note: The war itself ran 1817-1864 and includes the Circassian west; only the Imamate's years are listed. No zone is given because the Imamate's own land is the stake and the pages name no border districts, apart from the 1843 Avaria sweep in the ledger.

wars.name: Siege of Akhoulgo
wars.outcome: The siege 'claimed about 4,500 lives'; the page does not give the result or any territorial change.
wars.note: Akhulgo was one of Shamil's seats (infobox list).

wars.name: Shamil's 1843 offensive in Avaria
wars.outcome: Shamil's forces killed 486 at Untsukul on 28 August 1843 and 'took every Russian outpost in Avaria except one' in the next four weeks.
wars.note: Shamil's forces also 'withstood' Vorontsov's 1845 offensive, which the page places in 1845 without naming Dargo.

certainty.note: Mountain frontiers with no treaty or survey line; the Terek line of Russian forts and the Chechen plain were disputed ground.

notes:
Pages: Caucasian Imamate, Caucasian War (budget 1-2). The Imam Shamil, Siege of Akhoulgo, Battle of Dargo and Fall of Gunib pages were not opened: the Imamate's progress 1836-1858 (what Shamil held and lost, the Dargo expedition of 1845, Vedeno, Gunib) is therefore unverified; the 1836 and 1857 keyframes carry that flag.
End year: Cliopatria stops in 1858; the infobox says dissolved 1859, and the Caucasian War page puts Shamil's capture in 1859. The dossier ends in 1859 with a one-year keyframe. The exact surrender (6 September 1859 New Style) is not on either page.
Counterparts: 'avar-khanate' (Khanate of Avaria, Russian dependency whose capital was Khunzakh) has no dossier; it needs one from eu-19-x. The Imamate has no predecessor dossier ('Chechen Dominion' in the infobox is unclear) and appears on land the Russian Empire claimed; the Russian Empire dossier (eu-17) should carry a matching loss in 1843 (Avaria posts) and gain in 1859. Capital coordinates are approximate, from no page. The Circassian west (Adyghe tribes, 'extended authority west to the Adyghe (Circassian) tribes' via naibs) is not in the Cliopatria shape and not drawn; the page gives no date for it.
Gazetteer: no village names (Gimry, Khunzakh, Dargo, Vedeno, Akhulgo, Gunib, Untsukul) are in the gazetteer; the Avar disc uses a coordinate radius.
